newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close higher on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close higher on technical rebound.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended higher on a technical rebound following blue-chip buying by foreign insitutions, dealers and analysts said on Thursday.
The benchmark Composite index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 2.48 points to 1,215.03, while the small-capitalised Second Board index was off 2.79 to 616.48.
"The selling over the last two to three days has been unsubstantiated. Today has seen a technical rebound," said Faez Khairuddin, head of research at S.J. Securities.
"There has been some foreign buying of Tenaga and United Engineers," said a dealer at a local brokerage house.
Tenaga closed up 50 cents to 12.10 ringgit, and United Engineers ended 80 cents higher to 21.90 ringgit.
Telekom continued to slide, closing 30 cents down to 19.70. "We are continuing to sell Telekom. We estimate the fair value to be around 16 ringgit," said another dealer at the same house.
Telekom had been hit by continuing negative sentiment over the possibility of deregulation within the industry being brought forward.
Volume surged to 449 million shares traded, valued at 2,448 million ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 309 to 273.
